trials.notes: Passed 7/7. Chose `WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment()` for structure-aware traversal, used documented `next_tag()`, `is_tag_closer()`, `get_tag()`, `get_breadcrumbs()`, `add_class()`, and inherited `get_updated_html()`. The `tag_closers => visit` option is unnecessary for this task but documented and safely guarded.

Passed 7/7. Correct processor choice and no undocumented API calls: `next_token()`, `get_token_type()`, `is_tag_closer()`, `get_tag()`, `get_breadcrumbs()`, `add_class()`, `get_last_error()`, and `get_updated_html()` are documented. Slightly less direct than a tag-only walk, but the token filter is idiomatic and the `get_last_error()` fallback is conservative.

Passed 7/7. Uses the intended structural API: fragment processor, `next_tag()`, `get_breadcrumbs()` with current node excluded from the ancestor scan, `add_class()`, and `get_updated_html()`. The `is_tag_closer()` guard after plain `next_tag()` is redundant because closers are skipped by default, but harmless and documented.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial; all candidates passed all 7 frozen cases. The docs did well in the passages most relevant to this task: `Which processor should I use?` distinguishes the Tag Processor from the structure-aware HTML Processor; `create_fragment()` identifies body-fragment parsing and null creation; `next_tag()` documents scanning in source order and branching on `get_tag()` for multiple tag names; `Breadcrumbs` and `get_breadcrumbs()` explain the root-to-current path; `add_class()` plus `get_updated_html()` explain preserving existing classes and untouched bytes. Near-misses were minor: trials 1 and 3 defensively checked closers even where plain `next_tag()` skips them, and trial 2 relied on counting the current list in breadcrumbs rather than explicitly slicing ancestors. None indicate a documentation-caused failure here.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs state that breadcrumbs include the currently matched element, but ancestor-only checks are an easy off-by-one trap.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note and tiny snippet showing that callers should remove the final breadcrumb entry when asking questions about ancestors only.

doc_gaps.problem: `get_updated_html()` is essential after `add_class()` on an HTML Processor, but its full method documentation lives under the Tag Processor and is not surfaced as its own inherited method section in the HTML Processor docs.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an inherited `get_updated_html()` entry or short section to the HTML Processor docs stating that queued attribute/class/text edits are read with this method and untouched source bytes are preserved.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs mention `get_last_error()` and incomplete-token checks in several places, but the return policy after a structural walk that queues source-preserving edits is not gathered in one place.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short policy note for mutation passes: after walking with the HTML Processor, callers may fail closed on `get_last_error()` or truncation when their contract requires a complete structural scan; otherwise `get_updated_html()` returns queued edits without normalization.
